source_text: Quia ergo claret, imitationem malorum hominum non solum consequenter, sed et necessario dici; hoc interim argumentum tuum iacere perspicuum est. Quod vero addis, de diabolo esse scriptum: Imitantur eum, qui sunt ex parte ipsius [n58] ; et ego assentior dictum esse prudenter ab eo, quicumque libri ipsius auctor est; sed tibi non prodest, quod scribuntur quidam diaboli imitatione peccare, nisi docueris non posse hominum imitatione delinqui.
pass_a_gloss: Because therefore it is clear that imitation of evil human beings is said not only consequently but also necessarily; it is for the meantime perspicuous that this argument of yours lies fallen. But what you add, that of the devil it is written: They imitate him, who are from his party; I also assent that it was said prudently by him, whoever is the author of that book; but it does not profit you that some are written to sin by imitation of the devil, unless you have taught that it cannot be offended by imitation of human beings.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin

pass_b_english: It is clear, then, that imitation of evil human beings is not merely a consistent expression but a necessary one. For the moment, it is evident that this argument of yours lies defeated. You add that Scripture says of the devil, ‘Those who belong to his party imitate him’ (Wisdom 2:24; Latin numbering 2:25). I too agree that the author of that book, whoever he is, said this wisely. But the statement that some sin by imitating the devil does not help you unless you show that people cannot sin by imitating human beings.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
